title: Per-emission accounting with KV-cache-adjusted token timings
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Goal: Produce an attribution signal that maps every emitted token to a marginal latency and marginal cost contribution that accounts for: (1) whether the token was served from a KV cache hit, (2) batching effects during generation, and (3) downstream kernel/hardware variance. This ticket implements the per-emission accounting layer and the telemetry schema used by dashboards and billing reconciliation jobs.

Why: Current token-level metrics are coarse (per-request or sampled) and double-count cache savings or fail to credit cache hits correctly when batching reduces measured latency. Without a corrected per-emission ledger, Optimize recommendations and billing reconciliations show noisy, biased unit costs.

Scope (MVP):
- Instrument serving runtime to emit a PerEmission event for each token emitted by the runtime driver. Events should be light-weight and high-throughput (serialized protobuf/compact JSON), back-pressured to the telemetry pipeline.
- PerEmission event fields (MVP schema): emission_id, request_id, model, model_version, shard_id, emit_index (token index in sequence), timestamp_emit_start, timestamp_emit_end, kv_cache_status (HIT|MISS|PARTIAL), kv_cache_latency_ms, batch_window_ms, batch_size_at_emit, upstream_queue_ms, kernel_ms, cpu_ms, gpu_ms, effective_sequence_length, quantization_profile, fallback_variant (boolean), route_tag.
- Derived fields computed downstream: marginal_latency_ms (timestamp_emit_end - timestamp_emit_start minus shared batch overhead), cache_credit_ms (estimate of latency avoided due to KV hit), token_cost_units (raw compute cost bucket).
- Add a compact histogram/summary stream for very-high-throughput models (where emitting every token overwhelms the pipeline). This will send sampled PerEmission events (1/N) and per-request aggregated counters with sampling metadata.
- Expose new metrics and dashboards that: show distribution of marginal_latency_ms by model and route_tag, aggregate cache_credit_ms and cost savings per model-version, and surface drift where cache effectiveness drops over time.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
1) Emit vs sample: Full emission-level fidelity gives easiest attribution but increases pipeline volume. We will default to 1x emit for small models and sampling for large models (>500 reqs/s per shard). Sampling is deterministic (hash of request_id + model) so downstream remapping remains stable.
2) Attribution of shared batch overhead: We will measure batch_window_ms and upstream_queue_ms and apportion shared wait time equally across tokens in the batch by default. Future work may weight by token position or observed kernel hotspots.
3) KV cache credit: KV cache latency reduction is estimated by comparing observed kv_cache_latency_ms for HITs to historical miss baseline per model/seq-length percentiles. This avoids needing an exact simulated miss. We record kv_cache_status and raw latency to allow reprocessing when baselines improve.
4) Sampling consistency: Sampling metadata (sample_rate, sample_seed) must be included in event and request-level aggregation to allow unbiased downstream scaling.
5) Privacy/security: Events include no user prompt content or PII; request-level identifiers are hashed where possible. Security review not required for MVP but will be re-evaluated for Private deployments where telemetry egress rules differ.

Acceptance criteria:
- Runtime emits PerEmission events with all MVP schema fields for at least two test models (gpt-small and gpt-medium) behind feature flag.
- Telemetry pipeline (kafka -> processing -> bigtable/metrics store) ingests PerEmission payloads at test throughput of 5k eps with <10s ingestion P95.
- Dashboards: a) "Per-Emission Marginal Latency" showing p50/p95/p99 by model-version and route_tag; b) "KV Cache Credit" summarizing cumulative cache_credit_ms and estimated cost savings; c) "Sampling Health" showing sampling rate and estimated reconstruction error.
- Billing reconciliation job can use derived token_cost_units to produce a per-model per-day unit cost report within 2% of ground-truth offline replay for a 24-hour test window.

Implementation plan (high-level):
1) Add PerEmission event emitter in runtime emission path (PR: runtime#1876). Use a lock-free ring buffer sink to avoid blocking critical emission path; add backpressure token to degrade to sampling under overload.
2) Extend ingestion schema in telemetry pipeline: add kafka topic token-emission-v1 and a lightweight processor to compute derived fields and write to metrics store. Reuse existing per-token aggregation tools where possible.
3) Create sampled aggregation fallback for high-throughput model families.
4) Build dashboards and add to Console: key visualizations and export for Optimize.
5) Run a 2-week shadow run with feature-flagged production traffic, compare outputs with offline replay.

Risks and mitigations:
- Volume: Per-token events can blow up pipeline storage. Mitigate with deterministic sampling, compression, and TTLs.
- Attribution errors from batch apportioning: Validate apportionment heuristics against offline microbenchmarks that replay batched traces.
- Reprocessing complexity: Store raw kv_cache_latency_ms and sampling metadata so we can recompute credits retroactively if baselines change.

Open questions:
- Should we add a per-kernel tag (e.g., flash_attn_v2) to event now or in follow-up? (Currently opt to include kernel_ms and leave tag for later after kernel mapping stabilizes.)
- Do we propagate user-facing route tags (customer_tier) in every event? Risk: adds more cardinality. Proposal: include route_tag only when non-default.
